requirements.title: Unhandled end-of-file initiates error termination
requirements.definition: An EOF condition in an I/O statement containing neither END= nor IOSTAT= initiates error termination.

pending.eof-without-end-or-iostat-terminates: In a subprocess fixture, read beyond a one-record internal file without END= or IOSTAT= after first proving the first read succeeds; assert abnormal termination without comparing diagnostic text.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, named intrinsic status values where the standard names them, branch-target execution, or unchanged sentinel values where the source requires no definition. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific nonzero IOSTAT numbers are not asserted.

requirements.title: Handled end-of-file terminates input processing and defines status specifiers
requirements.definition: When EOF occurs with END= or IOSTAT= present and no error occurs, input-list processing terminates and IOSTAT= and IOMSG= specifiers that appear are defined as specified by their owning rules.

pending.handled-eof-input-processing-terminates: Use a one-record internal file, initialize a second input item to a nondefault sentinel, read past the end with IOSTAT=, and assert IOSTAT_END while avoiding any claim about the now-undefined item.
pending.handled-eof-iostat-defined: Initialize IOSTAT to zero, read beyond a one-record internal file with IOSTAT=, and assert the named constant IOSTAT_END, not its numeric value.
pending.handled-eof-iomsg-defined: No portable oracle compares IOMSG text or proves an assigned message differs from a sentinel; future EOF tests use IOSTAT_END/END= for portable observation.

requirements.title: Handled end-of-file makes transfer do-variables and input items undefined
requirements.definition: For a data transfer statement or wait-operation EOF, do-variables in the initiating statement become undefined; for input-initiated EOF, all effective input items or namelist objects in the initiating statement become undefined.

pending.handled-eof-do-variables-undefined: No portable oracle may inspect a do-variable that the source makes undefined; future EOF tests do not use it after the condition.
pending.handled-eof-input-items-undefined: No portable oracle may inspect effective input items or namelist objects that the source makes undefined; future tests reinitialize them before subsequent checks.

requirements.title: EOF on an external record file positions the file after the endfile record
requirements.definition: If the input statement specifies an external record file, handled EOF positions the file after the endfile record.

pending.handled-eof-external-record-position-aft: Write a sequential external record followed by ENDFILE, read to EOF with IOSTAT_END, then BACKSPACE once and read again; observing EOF again checks the after-endfile position without depending on marker representation.

requirements.title: END= branches on handled end-of-file
requirements.definition: If an END= specifier appears for handled EOF, execution branches to the statement with the specified label.

pending.handled-eof-end-branch: Initialize a marker to a nonmatching sentinel, read beyond a one-record internal file with END= and IOSTAT=, set the marker only at the END target, and assert the marker and IOSTAT_END.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.10.3-12.12: IOLENGTH, error, end-of-record and end-of-file conditions, IOSTAT=, IOMSG=, and restrictions on I/O statements (batch166). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer, accepted with no findings. IOLENGTH's exact count is latitude but its direct-access RECL= suitability is planned; END=/EOR= conditions, IOSTAT_END and IOSTAT_EOR distinctness, zero on success and positive errors are planned portably; IOMSG unchanged on success is planned with a sentinel while condition-message text is never compared. Source accounting only.
